from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Borsuk-Ulam states spheres map to R-n.",
            "Antipodal points share the same value.",
            "Earth has two opposite spots with identical weather."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Borsuk-Ulam states spheres map to R-n.
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.2, color="#3498DB", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, "C3")
        self.play(Create(sphere))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Antipodal points share the same value.
        # Antipodal points
        point_a = Dot(color="#E74C3C").move_to(sphere.get_center() + np.array([1.2, 0, 0]))
        point_b = Dot(color="#E74C3C").move_to(sphere.get_center() + np.array([-1.2, 0, 0]))
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(point_a, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(point_b, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(point_a), Create(point_b), Write(label_a), Write(label_b))
        
        # Flash / Pulse to indicate equal value
        self.play(
            point_a.animate.set_color("#F1C40F").scale(1.5),
            point_b.animate.set_color("#F1C40F").scale(1.5),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            point_a.animate.set_color("#E74C3C").scale(1/1.5),
            point_b.animate.set_color("#E74C3C").scale(1/1.5)
        )
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Earth has two opposite spots with identical weather.
        # Deform the sphere
        sphere_deformed = Sphere(radius=1.2, color="#9B59B6", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere_deformed, "C3")
        
        self.play(Transform(sphere, sphere_deformed))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Topology helps us solve discrete problems.", "Necklaces represent linear, ordered resource sets.", "Cuts divide these sets into fair shares."]
        self.setup_layout("Transition: From Geometry to Combinatorics", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Represent the geometric sphere as a discrete grid, color #BDC3C7.
        sphere_grid = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.5, color="#BDC3C7") for _ in range(16)]).arrange_in_grid(4, 4, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(sphere_grid, 'A1', 'C3')
        self.play(Create(sphere_grid))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#BDC3C7"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transform the continuous antipodal mapping into a combinatorial rule.
        necklace = Line(start=self.grid['D1'], end=self.grid['D6'], color=WHITE)
        beads = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1, color=GOLD if i % 2 == 0 else GREY).move_to(necklace.point_from_proportion(i/10)) for i in range(11)])
        self.add(necklace, beads)
        self.play(FadeIn(necklace), FadeIn(beads))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#BDC3C7"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the shift to discrete binary choice, color #E67E22.
        cut = Line(start=self.grid['C4'] + UP*0.5, end=self.grid['E4'] + DOWN*0.5, color="#E67E22")
        self.play(Create(cut))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#E67E22"))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Two thieves split a mixed bead necklace.",
            "K plus S cuts ensure fair division.",
            "Each thief receives identical bead types.",
            "Raccoons demonstrate equal distribution of resources.",
            "Fairness is guaranteed by simple cutting math."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Stolen Necklace Problem", lecture_lines)
        
        # Necklace of beads (10 gold, 10 silver)
        beads = VGroup()
        for i in range(20):
            color = GOLD if i % 2 == 0 else GREY
            dot = Dot(color=color)
            beads.add(dot)
        beads.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(beads, 'C1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(beads)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#F39C12"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#E74C3C"))
        # Visualize cuts
        cuts = VGroup()
        for i in [5, 15]:
            line = Line(start=UP*0.5, end=DOWN*0.5, color=RED).move_to(beads[i].get_center())
            cuts.add(line)
        self.play(Create(cuts))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#2ECC71"))
        # Show division
        self.play(beads[5:15].animate.shift(DOWN*1.5))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))
        # Raccoon placeholders
        raccoon1 = Text("R1", color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid['E2'])
        raccoon2 = Text("R2", color=YELLOW).move_to(self.grid['E5'])
        self.play(Write(raccoon1), Write(raccoon2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem: Fairness in a Divided World
outline.target_audience: University students with a background in basic calculus and set theory

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Continuous Mapping
sections.content: Define a continuous function from a sphere (Sⁿ) to Euclidean space (Rⁿ). Visualize this as mapping points on a globe onto a flat map without tearing the surface.
sections.example: Imagine drawing a rubber sheet (the sphere) and stretching it onto a flat surface; if you don't rip it, the mapping is continuous.

sections.title: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem (The Core Concept)
sections.content: Introduce the theorem: For any continuous function from a sphere Sⁿ to Rⁿ, there exists at least one pair of antipodal points (opposite sides of the sphere) that map to the same value.
sections.example: The 'Temperature-Pressure' example: At any given moment on Earth, there must be two exactly opposite points with the exact same temperature and air pressure.

sections.title: Transition: From Geometry to Combinatorics
sections.content: Explain how the topological properties of the Borsuk-Ulam theorem allow us to solve discrete problems, specifically fair division (The Necklace Splitting Theorem).
sections.example: Visualizing a necklace with two types of beads (e.g., gold and silver) stretched across a line, seeking the minimum cuts needed to share it fairly.

sections.title: The Stolen Necklace Problem
sections.content: Present the problem: Two thieves steal a necklace with 2k gold beads and 2s silver beads. How many cuts are needed to divide the spoils equally? The theorem proves that k+s cuts are always sufficient.
sections.example: Two anthropomorphic raccoons trying to split a string of 10 gold beads and 10 silver beads. Show them finding the exact spots to cut so both get an identical share of each bead type.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Significance
sections.content: Synthesize how abstract topology guarantees fairness in resource allocation. Reinforce that mathematical constraints can force 'equal outcomes' in complex, multi-variable environments.
sections.example: Application to modern economics: Distributing assets in a divorce or dividing computing tasks across multiple servers to ensure load balancing.
